The relevant facts, in short, are that the opposite party No.3 (hereinafter called the plaintiff) as plaintiffs instituted partition suit No. 89 of 1996 praying for saham of 1/4 share in the suit property according to partition deed No. 160 dated 23-12-1958. It is contended that on the basis of partition deed No. 160 dated 23-12-1958, the plaintiff got 1(c) schedule property in his saham, defendant Ibrahim got 4(B) schedule land, defendant Afzal Khan got 3(B) schedule land and defendant Azmal Khan got 5(B) schedule land as their respective share from the Suit property. Before the execution of partition deed dated 23-12-1958 suit land was rented to SVOC Petrol Pump and all the 4 brothers were enjoying possession according to their respective share through tenants. Subsequently, the schedule land was rerited by a tenancy agreement to Esso Standard Eastern Co. for constructing a petrol pump and after liberation the said petrol pump was transferred to Meghna Petroleum Co. Ltd, and thereafter, the plaintiff gave a power of attorney in favour of his brother opposite party No. 1 Azmal Khan to look after his share on his behalf. But subsequently, for certain misdeeds, the plaintiff having been dissatisfied with the opposite party No.1, requested Meghna Petroleum to execute a new tenancy agreement with him for 1/4 his share of the suit land and thereafter also served a notice through his lawyer after expiry of tenancy agreement dated 31-10-1990 and, in fact, no tenancy agreement was executed with him Accordingly, the plaintiff as owner of 1/4 share of the suit land has not been getting due share of the rent as heirs by, metes and bounds, so the plaintiff asked all other share holders to get the suit land divided for getting their due shares except the opposite party No. 1 as defendant No. 2 having been in advantageous position in joint ownership suit land denying to give their due shares. Hence the suit. 

 4. After filing of the written statement dated. 27-7-1997 the trial of the suit started and thereafter at the belated stage the defendant-opposite party No. 1 filed the additional written statement on 10-4-2003 stating that the partition agreement dated 23-12-1958 regarding purchase of the suit land by a kabala dated 30-10-48 is false, baseless and collusive, etc. Furthermore, after having been examined by the trial Court the defendant-opposite party No. 1 filed another petition praying for amendment of his written statement under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating that due to ill health he ,could not properly advise his appointed lawyer about his fight, title and possession in the suit property and, as such, some material facts were not correctly stated in the written statement and therefore some mistakes are necessary to be amended in the interest of justice otherwise, he will suffer irreparable loss and injury. 

 9. Mr Mahmudul Hoque, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioner, submits that the impugned order dated 20-7-2003 is a nonspeaking order and the learned trial Court without assigning any reason whatsoever allowed the application in a summary manner which is illegal and beyond the scope of law. The learned Advocate, referring to written statement, additional written statement and amendment petition (Annexure-A, B and C to the main Revisional Petition) filed by the defendant opposite party No.1, submits that the averments made in the written statement itself reflects the same is apparently inconsistent and contradictory with the additional written statements inasmuch as in the additional' statement the defendant-opposite party No. 1 falsely stated that the partition deed No. 160 dated 23-12-1958 is false, fraudulent, void and not acted upon and the same was not signed and executed by him etc. but in fact, he admitted the partition deed dated 23-12-1958 in his earlier written statement (Annexure-A) and hence' the order of allowing the additional written statements cannot be sustained in law. Mr Md Mahmudul Hoque, the learned Advocate, further submits that the learned trial Court failed to appreciate that the prayer for additional written statement and proposed amendment is a deviation from the earlier taken by the opposite party No. 1 in his original written statement, inasmuch as in his earlier written statement (Annexure A) he categorically admitted the partition deed No. 140 dated 23-12-1958 but in the proposed amendment a new story has been set up changing the main issues of the case at a very belated stage of the suit, which cannot be said to be just and necessary for the purpose of determining the real controversy between the parties and, as such, the learned Joint District Judge by passing the instant impugned order committed an error of law as well as facts in issues and resulted an error in its decision occasioning failure of justice which warrants interference by this Court. Finally, the learned Advocate most emphatically submits that the deposition made by the defendant-opposite party No.1, before the trial Court introducing a new story which is contradictory and inconsistent with his earlier pleadings but the trial Court overlooking this aspect mechanically rejected the petitioner's application for expunging the deposition of defendant-opposite party No.1, as outside of his written statement. In support of his submissions the learned Advocate has relied on some decisions reported in 46 DLR (AD) 130, 51DLR 420, 44DLR 69,34 DLR 278, 1992 BLD 591, 41 DLR 190, 15 DLR 315,46 DLR 273, PLD 1982 (Kar) 111, 46 DLR 57, AIR 1961 (Born) 136, AIR 1953 (Cal) 15. 

 11. We have heard the learned Advocate of both the side at length and persused impugned order and other tangible materials on record. It appears that the real question in controversy in the suit was for partition of the suit properties in between the co- sharers according to partition deed No. 160 dated 23-12-1958, whereas the issue raised in the amendment application is claiming exclusive title and possession in the suit property after denying existence of admitted partition deed dated 23-12-1958; It also appears that in this case the original written statement was filed much earlier i.e. on 27-7-1997, and after a long lapse of 6 years an application for amendment of the written statement was filed on 10-4-2003 and within that long 6 years PWs and DWs including defendant-opposite party No. 1 himself having been examined and cross- examined before the trial Court apparently a new story was attempted to be added in the additional written statement stating exclusive ownership, possession and control in the suit property by giving a go-bye to the earlier pleadings of joint property equally belonging to this petitioner and other opposite parties as per Partition Deed No. 160 dated 23-12-1958. As a matter of fact, no papers and documents were annexed with the additional written statement and the amendment application showing exclusive ownership of the defendant No.2 in the suit land. Furthermore, ongoing through the impugned order dated 20-7-2003 it appears that the learned joint district judge without assigning any reason whatsoever allowed the application for additional statement and prayer for amendment of written statement filed by the defendant No.2. Mr Mahmudul Hoque, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, has cited a number of decisions as stated above, to show that the prayer for amendment of written statement and prayer for additional written statement should not be allowed, if it is found malafide, belated, inconsistent in character and that does not relate to the real point in controversy. In the case reported in 34 DLR 278 the governing consideration was that according to the provisions under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code the parties after filing their pleadings they will not be allowed to depart from the pleadings or raise any new allegation of fact inconsistent with the previous pleadings.  13. Mr Mahmudul Hoque, the learned Advocate, in course of argument, has taken us through the written statement and deposition of defendant-apposite party No. 1(Annexure-A & L-1) and submits that a party cannot adduce evidence unless he pleads his case in the pleadings. In this case there being no specific demand of the assertion of the plaintiffs with regard to their partition deed dated 23-12-1958 and joint ownership, of the suit property by way of inheritance in the written statement filed by the defendant opposite party No.1, but subsequently, shifting his earlier stand introduced a new story in his deposition before the Court denying the contention of the said partition deed dated 23-12-1958 but the plaintiff instituted the suit for partition according to the terms of registered partition deed dated 23-12-1958. and therefore, inconsistent and contradictory portion of testimony of the defendant opposite party No. 1 should be expunged.  16. Having regard to the foregoing discussions and observations, we are of the view that additional written statement filed on 10-4-2003 and an application for amendment of written statement filled on 10-5-2003 (Annexure B&C) by the opposite party No. 1 claiming his alleged exclusive title and possession in the suit land by Kabala dated 30-1-1948, denying the admitted partition Deed No. 160 dated 23-12-1958 to depart from earlier pleadings .incorporated by the opposite party No.1 (defendant No.2) in his original written statement dated 27-7- 97 with sole motive of harassing and causing financial loss to the, petitioner and other co-sharers by dragging the matter for an indefinite period and it also appears that the opposite party No. 1 (defendant No.2) in his deposition introduced a new and inconsistent story beyond his pleadings which is prohibited under the provisions of Order VI, rule 17 of the Civil Procedure Code. Moreover, on perusal of the said applications dated 10-4-2003 and 10-5- 2003 (Annexures B & C) filed by the opposite party No. 1 it becomes clear that a new claim and new allegations of facts, raised subsequently by the opposite party No. 1 are totally inconsistent with his earlier pleadings or a go-bye to his earlier pleadings/ case of joint property belonging to this petitioner and defendant-opposite parties equally by partition deed dated 23-12-1958. So, in the given facts and circumstances of the case and in view of the provisions of Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the uniform decisions of the highest Court as cited above, we are constrained to hold that the learned trial Court ought to have held that the additional written statement and the amendment petition (Annexures B & C) filed by the opposite party No. 1 (defendant No.2) are not bonafide rather malafide.
